The user wants me to summarize the Live Server VS Code extension and determine if it would be useful based on their workspace and workflow.## Live Server Extension Summary

**Live Server** (`ritwickdey.liveserver`) launches a local development server with live reload for static and dynamic pages. When you save an HTML, CSS, or JS file, the browser automatically refreshes.

### Key Features
- One-click launch from the status bar or right-click menu
- Auto-reload on file save (uses WebSocket injection)
- Configurable port, root folder, and browser
- HTTPS support, custom middleware, proxy
- Works with any static HTML/CSS/JS project

### Relevance to Your Workspace

Looking at your projects, you have several HTML-based projects that would benefit:

| Project | Structure | Benefit |
|---------|-----------|---------|
| **contractor-portal/** | `index.html` + `css/` + `js/` | Direct fit — static HTML site, no build tool |
| **contractor-portal-dataverse/** | Node.js Express (`server.js`) + `public/` | Less useful — already has its own Express server |
| **code-apps/** | Vite + React + TypeScript | Not needed — Vite's `npm run dev` has built-in HMR which is superior |

### Recommendation

**Moderately useful.** Your main beneficiary is the **contractor-portal** project (plain HTML/CSS/JS with no server). Live Server would give you instant browser refresh while editing it. However, your other web projects either have their own dev servers (Express, Vite) or aren't web frontends at all (Python scripts, Logic Apps ARM templates, Power Apps).

If you find yourself frequently editing the contractor-portal or similar static HTML files and want auto-refresh without spinning up a server manually, it's worth installing. Otherwise, it's not essential given your stack.
